issues.legal_issue: The court that passed a decree for specific performance may consider an application to extend the time for payment when it is also the executing court.
material_facts: The decrees for specific performance required the purchasers to deposit the balance consideration within a specified period.
The purchasers sought extensions after the deposit deadline had passed, and the applications were sent to the executing court, which was the court where the original suits had been filed.
issues.conclusion: The court that passed the decree retains jurisdiction to extend the time for compliance, and where that court is also the executing court it may consider the application in the execution proceedings, treating it as an application in the original suit.
issues.legal_principle: Section 28 of the Specific Relief Act, 1963, permits the court to extend the time for payment after a decree for specific performance and does not make the court functus officio. Under Ramankutty Guptan v. Avara, an application under Section 28 may be made in the executing court when it is the same court that passed the decree; Sardar Mohar Singh v. Mangilal likewise recognizes the court's continuing power to extend time.

predicates.specific_performance_decree: The proceeding concerns execution of a decree requiring performance of a contract for the sale or lease of immovable property.
predicates.extension_application_after_decree: The party required to make payment applies for more time after the decree has been made.
predicates.original_court_is_executing_court: The court handling execution is the same court in which the original suit was filed and the decree was passed.

issues.definition: When a post-decree extension application arises in a specific-performance proceeding and the original court is handling execution, that court may consider the application.

issues.legal_issue: A court should not extend the time for payment under a specific-performance decree as a matter of course when the decree-holder has substantially delayed compliance without explanation or fault by the opposing party.
material_facts: The decrees required the purchasers to deposit the balance consideration by a specified date, but one purchaser deposited it much later and the other did not deposit it.
The purchasers sought extensions years after the decrees and after the appeals had been dismissed; they had not sought an extension in the trial court within the time fixed by the decrees.
No explanation was given for the failure to pay on time, and the purchasers did not claim that any act of the vendors prevented payment.
The High Court directed the executing court to consider the extension applications and suggested that the purchasers might have waited until the appeals ended or until execution was sought.
issues.conclusion: The extension applications should be refused; the High Court's judgment was set aside and the executing court's dismissal of the execution applications was confirmed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 28 of the Specific Relief Act, 1963, gives the court discretion to extend time, not an obligation to do so automatically. Section 16(c) requires a specific-performance plaintiff to aver and prove performance or continuing readiness and willingness to perform essential contractual terms. Specific performance is equitable and discretionary: the court must assess the party's conduct, the circumstances of delay, and whether compliance was prevented by the other party. K. Kalpana Saraswathi v. P.S.S. Somasundaram Chettiar recognizes the power to extend time while emphasizing equitable terms; K.S. Vidyanadam v. Vairavan, Chand Rani v. Kamal Rani, and N.P. Thirugnanam v. R. Jagan Mohan Rao address reasonable performance, conduct, and readiness and willingness; Ramankutty Guptan v. Avara addresses the court's continuing jurisdiction under Section 28.

rule.if: specific_performance_execution and payment_deadline_missed and extension_sought_after_substantial_delay and no_explanation_for_default and no_opposing_party_caused_obstacle

predicates.specific_performance_execution: The proceeding concerns execution of a decree requiring performance of a contract for the sale or lease of immovable property.
predicates.payment_deadline_missed: The decree-holder did not pay the required amount within the time fixed by the decree.
predicates.extension_sought_after_substantial_delay: The decree-holder sought more time only after a substantial period had passed since the payment deadline.
predicates.no_explanation_for_default: The decree-holder gave no explanation for failing to make payment within the time fixed by the decree.
predicates.no_opposing_party_caused_obstacle: The decree-holder did not show that the opposing party caused an obstacle that prevented timely payment.

issues.definition: In execution of a specific-performance decree, a missed payment deadline followed by substantially delayed, unexplained noncompliance not caused by the opposing party results in denial of an extension.
